scope: Read sources for the convention contract, sphere coordinates, angular construction, zodiacal and mundane body directions, and M7 timing keys; numerical expectations are separately hand-derived.

sources.author: Claudius Ptolemy
sources.title: Tetrabiblos
sources.locator: Book III, chapter XIV, printed pages 94-96
sources.excerpt: each equatorial degree being taken to signify one solar year
supports: Equatorial arc to solar-year mapping attributed to Ptolemy.
Proportional temporal-hour construction using the appropriate diurnal or nocturnal hourly times.
Printed page 94 distinguishes rising by ascensional times, meridian by right ascensions and setting by descensions.
sources.m4Reading: Reread HTML angular construction on printed page 94, 2026-10-14.
sources.m7Reading: Reread the fetched HTML transcription on 2026-10-14, printed page 94: an equatorial degree signifies one solar year. No modern elapsed-day length is specified.

sources.author: Placidus de Titis
sources.title: Primum Mobile
sources.locator: Printed pages 17-23, theses 40, 45-46, 55, 60-61; page 57; pages 104-105, canon XXXVII
sources.excerpt: a proportional division of the diurnal and nocturnal arcs, and no other way.
supports: Mundane positions and aspects use proportional diurnal and nocturnal arcs; bodily latitude is retained.
Direct carries the promissor westward to the fixed position of the significator.
Converse applies the significator's rules to the promissor and vice versa.
The author rejects converse directions of angles and converse zodiacal aspects.
Thesis 61 also excludes zodiacal rays to angles; the angle primitive enables conjunctions only.
sources.m4Reading: Reread fetched PDF text in memory, 2026-10-14: printed page 57 (PDF page index 73), thesis 60 on printed page 23, canon XXXVII on printed page 105. Direct westward motion and converse angle prohibition confirmed.
sources.m5Reading: Fetched PDF and extracted text in memory on 2026-10-14. Read printed pages 23-24, 57-61, 68-69 and 104-105; PDF page numbers are printed numbers plus 17. Canon XIX uses the promissor aspect place's semi-arc to scale the fixed significator's meridian distance.
m5Limits: Zero-both is a project projection restriction, not the changing significator latitude in canon XXIII.
The general semi-arc model does not implement the Sun's special treatment below the horizon in canons XX-XXI.
Canon XXXVII supplies mundane converse role exchange. No converse zodiacal construction, including projected conjunctions, is enabled.
sources.m6Reading: Fetched PDF and read extracted text in memory on 2026-10-14. Part III printed pages 72-73; canons XXVII-XXVIII, pages 74-77; canons XXX-XXXII, pages 87-91; canon XXXVI, pages 98-104; canon XXXVII, pages 104-105. PDF page numbers are printed numbers plus 17.
m6Supports: Mundane aspects divide the diurnal and nocturnal arcs proportionally; classical aspect separations are expressed through mundane houses.

Canon XXX retains both bodily latitudes for conjunction. Canon XXXII scales distance within a house by horary times, using the moving body's diurnal or nocturnal time according to its position at contact.
Canon XXXVII carries the original significator to the original promissor's fixed mundane position or rays in converse, exchanging the horary-time ratio.
m6Limits: Westward and eastward branch names are explicit project coordinate labels, measured from original promissor to original significator; they do not silently import zodiacal ray terminology.
The uniform ordinary semi-arc construction does not implement canon XXXVI's special solar crepuscular treatment, mundane parallels or minor aspects.
Body significators on axes do not extend the method to converse angular significators.

sources.author: William Lilly
sources.title: Christian Astrology
supports: The caster's sinister ray follows sign order; its dexter ray runs against sign order.
Aries casts sextile, square and trine sinister to Gemini, Cancer and Leo, and dexter to Aquarius, Capricorn and Sagittarius.
notEstablished: Lilly's branch terminology is not used as a substitute for Placidus's semi-arc geometry.

sources.author: Claudius Ptolemy
sources.title: Tetrabiblos
sources.locator: Book I, chapter XVI, printed pages 24-26
supports: Sextile, square, trine and opposition correspond to 60, 90, 120 and 180 degrees of the zodiac.

sources.author: US Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department
sources.title: Computing Altitude and Azimuth from Greenwich Apparent Sidereal Time
sources.locator: Local hour angle and altitude equations
supports: Local hour angle equals local sidereal angle minus right ascension after converting both to degrees.
Sine altitude is cos(hour angle) cos(declination) cos(latitude) plus sin(declination) sin(latitude).
notEstablished: The proportional coordinate, direction system and timing key are not defined by this source.

sources.author: William Lilly
sources.title: Christian Astrology
sources.locator: Chapter CLXVI, printed pages 709-715; PDF pages 223-229 (one-based)
sources.excerpt: the apparent diurnall motion of the Sun for the next day and same hour
supports: Ptolemy's degree/year key and Naibod's timing method are discussed separately.
Lilly attributes to Antonius Maginus a key using the Sun's right ascension at birth and at the same hour the following day.
That natal-day right-ascension difference is used as a fixed annual arc.
notEstablished: The rounded Naibod tables do not establish the exact 59 minutes 8.33 seconds rate used by this project; that explicit decimal is separately sourced to Kuhr.
Maginus's own text was not independently fetched and read.
The passage does not select a modern UTC, UT1 or TT day convention, a modern equator/equinox frame, or a canonical right-ascension unwrapping algorithm.
sources.m7Reading: Reread fetched PDF on 2026-10-14: printed page 709 for the Ptolemy mapping; page 710, The Practice, for the birth-to-next-day right-ascension difference; pages 712-715 for the Naibod discussion and rounded calendar conversion tables. The solar annual rate is held fixed rather than resampled at each age.

sources.author: Erich Carl Kühr
sources.title: Berechnung der Ereigniszeiten
sources.edition: Regulus-Verlag, Görlitz, 1936; year read on the scan title page
sources.formatRead: Fetched PDF and extracted text in memory; no PDF, chart or source table retained
sources.locator: Direktions-Schlüssel, printed pages 62-63, PDF page 37 (one-based); title page on PDF page 2
supports: Printed page 62 equates 59 minutes 8.33 seconds of equatorial arc to one year; page 63 identifies that derivation as the Naibod key.
The project preserves that printed decimal as a fixed conventional rate: 354833/360000 equatorial degrees per symbolic year.
notEstablished: Naibod's original text was not fetched and read; this source supplies Kuhr's explicit formulation.
This rounded published decimal is not an exact physical astronomical rate or a definition of an elapsed civil year.
Kuhr's directional geometry and predictive claims are outside the adopted source scope.
